title: Per-language repair playbook for SDK errors and streaming recovery
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: SDK consumers struggle to map low-level runtime failures to concrete remediation steps. Streaming operations compound the issue because partial progress is often lost and client authors are uncertain when to resume, retry, or fallback. This ticket delivers a per-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) "repair playbook": standardized error envelope, stable error codes, short human-readable recovery blurb, and language-specific quick-fix snippets for common failure classes (transient network, upstream model OOM, auth/KMS failures, and stream checkpoint/resume hints). The goal is consistent developer UX across SDKs and measurable reduction in support tickets and mean time to recovery for production incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact error envelope spec (error_code, stable_id, retriable:true/false, retry_after_seconds optional, short_recovery_hint) and commit spec doc to Confluence.
Expose the envelope across Python/TS/Go SDKs with identical field names and small ergonomic wrappers for idiomatic handling.
Provide streaming helper primitives: StreamCheckpoint(token), ResumeFrom(token) and examples demonstrating checkpointing mid-stream and safe retry with idempotency notes for each language.
Ship unit + integration tests that simulate network flaps, token expiry, and model OOM and assert error_code mapping and presence of short_recovery_hint.
Publish three one-page quickstart guides (Python/TS/Go) and two reproducible PR demos showing developer fix patterns for the top 5 errors reported by support in last 90 days.
Telemetry: errors emitted include stable_id and context tags so Console can surface a guided remediation link. Verify telemetry tag is present in a staging trace capture.
Backward compatibility: SDKs continue to return legacy error text in a transitional layer while the new envelope is preferred. Document migration steps.
Ship SDK patch release with release notes and migration examples by release date.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Draft the error envelope RFC and internal examples (this ticket).
Week 2: Sign-off with SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Platform/Telemetry teams; carve telemetry tag names and stable_id format.
Week 3-4: Implement language bindings and streaming helpers; add unit tests and local e2e harness that injects failures.
Week 5: Run canary with beta customers on dedicated instances; capture telemetry and iterate wording of short_recovery_hint.
Week 6: Docs, release notes, and library releases (patches) with migration guide.
examples_proposed: Streaming checkpoint pattern: emit StreamCheckpoint(token) at safe boundaries (sentence end or after N tokens) and include token in telemetry so ResumeFrom(token) can be verified in a trace.
